lesson_scope: Tangents and normals at a point: differentiate, evaluate the curve gradient, use the tangent or negative-reciprocal normal gradient, form a line, and obtain an axis intercept or genuine second intersection when requested.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: finding the gradient of a tangent to a polynomial curve by evaluating the derivative at a point.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of evaluating the derivative at a specific x-value to obtain tangent gradient.

hints: Differentiate the curve $y = 2x^3 - 5x + 4$ with respect to $x$ using the power rule.
Substitute $x = 2$ into the derivative: $m_T = 6(2)^2 - 5 = 6(4) - 5 = 19$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the curve $y = 2x^3 - 5x + 4$ to obtain the gradient function:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 6x^2 - 5$$

Substitute the given coordinate $x = 2$ into the gradient function:
$$m = \left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=2} = 6(2)^2 - 5 = 6(4) - 5$$

Calculate the final numerical gradient:
$$m = 24 - 5 = 19$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: calculating the normal gradient using the negative-reciprocal relation to the tangent gradient.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of the perpendicular normal gradient formula m_N = -1 / m_T.

hints: Rewrite $y = \dfrac{12}{x}$ as $y = 12x^{-1}$ and differentiate: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -12x^{-2} = -\dfrac{12}{x^2}$.
Substitute $x = 3$ to find the tangent gradient: $m_T = -\dfrac{12}{3^2} = -\dfrac{12}{9} = -\dfrac{4}{3}$.
Use the perpendicular condition $m_N = -\dfrac{1}{m_T}$ to find the normal gradient: $m_N = -\dfrac{1}{-4/3} = \dfrac{3}{4}$.

walkthrough.text:
Rewrite the curve equation in index form and differentiate:
$$y = 12x^{-1} \implies \frac{dy}{dx} = -12x^{-2} = -\frac{12}{x^2}$$

Find the gradient of the tangent $m_T$ at $x = 3$:
$$m_T = -\frac{12}{3^2} = -\frac{12}{9} = -\frac{4}{3}$$

Apply the perpendicular gradient relationship $m_N = -\dfrac{1}{m_T}$ to determine the normal gradient:
$$m_N = -\frac{1}{-4/3} = \frac{3}{4}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates to find tangent gradient $m_T = -\dfrac{12}{3^2} = -\dfrac{4}{3}$ and uses $m_N = -\dfrac{1}{m_T}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: writing the point-slope equation of a tangent line given the curve and point of contact.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of constructing tangent lines using y - y1 = m(x - x1).

hints: Find the derivative: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x - 4$.
Substitute the $x$-coordinate $x = 3$ to find the tangent slope: $m = 2(3) - 4 = 2$.
Use the line equation $y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)$ with point $(3, 4)$ and $m = 2$: $y - 4 = 2(x - 3) \implies y = 2x - 2$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate $y = x^2 - 4x + 7$ to find the gradient formula:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x - 4$$

Evaluate the gradient at $x = 3$:
$$m = 2(3) - 4 = 6 - 4 = 2$$

Form the tangent equation using the point-slope form with point $(3, 4)$:
$$y - 4 = 2(x - 3)$$
$$y - 4 = 2x - 6 \implies y = 2x - 2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds tangent gradient $m = 2(3) - 4 = 2$ and sets up line through $(3, 4)$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: writing the point-slope equation of a normal line to a quadratic curve.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of forming normal lines using perpendicular gradients.

hints: Differentiate $y = 3x^2 - 5x + 1$ to get $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 6x - 5$.
Find the tangent gradient at $x = 1$: $m_T = 6(1) - 5 = 1$.
Find the normal gradient: $m_N = -\dfrac{1}{1} = -1$.
Set up the line equation with $(1, -1)$: $y - (-1) = -1(x - 1) \implies y + 1 = -x + 1 \implies y = -x$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the curve to find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 6x - 5$$

Evaluate the tangent gradient $m_T$ and the perpendicular normal gradient $m_N$ at $x = 1$:
$$m_T = 6(1) - 5 = 1 \implies m_N = -\frac{1}{m_T} = -1$$

Form the normal equation using point $(1, -1)$:
$$y - (-1) = -1(x - 1)$$
$$y + 1 = -x + 1 \implies y = -x \quad (\text{or } x + y = 0)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds tangent gradient $m_T = 1 \implies m_N = -1$ and sets up normal line through $(1, -1)$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: determining the x-axis intercept of a tangent to a radical curve.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of finding coordinate axis intercepts of tangent lines.

hints: Differentiate $y = 4x^{1/2}$ to get $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x^{-1/2} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{x}}$.
At $(4, 8)$, the slope is $m = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{4}} = \dfrac{2}{2} = 1$.
Form the tangent equation: $y - 8 = 1(x - 4) \implies y = x + 4$.
Set $y = 0$ to find the $x$-intercept: $0 = x + 4 \implies x = -4$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the curve $y = 4x^{1/2}$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 4\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)x^{-1/2} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{x}}$$

Evaluate the tangent gradient at $x = 4$:
$$m = \frac{2}{\sqrt{4}} = \frac{2}{2} = 1$$

Form the tangent line equation at $(4, 8)$:
$$y - 8 = 1(x - 4) \implies y = x + 4$$

Find the $x$-coordinate of the $x$-intercept by setting $y = 0$:
$$0 = x + 4 \implies x = -4$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds tangent gradient $m = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{4}} = 1$ and forms tangent equation $y - 8 = 1(x - 4)$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: determining the y-axis intercept of a normal line to a composite power curve.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of finding normal line intercepts on coordinate axes.

hints: Use the chain rule on $y = (2x - 1)^2$ to find $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2(2x - 1)(2) = 4(2x - 1)$.
At $x = 2$, the tangent slope is $m_T = 4(2(2) - 1) = 4(3) = 12$.
The normal slope is $m_N = -\dfrac{1}{12}$. Form the normal equation: $y - 9 = -\dfrac{1}{12}(x - 2)$.
Set $x = 0$ to find the $y$-intercept: $y = 9 + \dfrac{2}{12} = 9 + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{55}{6}$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate $y = (2x - 1)^2$ using the linear chain rule:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 2(2x - 1)^1 \times 2 = 4(2x - 1)$$

Evaluate the tangent gradient and normal gradient at $(2, 9)$:
$$m_T = 4(2(2) - 1) = 4(3) = 12 \implies m_N = -\frac{1}{12}$$

Form the equation of the normal line at $(2, 9)$:
$$y - 9 = -\frac{1}{12}(x - 2)$$

Find the $y$-coordinate of the $y$-intercept $B$ by setting $x = 0$:
$$y - 9 = -\frac{1}{12}(0 - 2) \implies y - 9 = \frac{2}{12} = \frac{1}{6} \implies y = 9 + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{55}{6}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds normal gradient $m_N = -\dfrac{1}{12}$ and forms normal equation $y - 9 = -\dfrac{1}{12}(x - 2)$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: a direct polynomial derivative and a tangent line are used in one short, ordered intercept calculation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source supplies the tangent-gradient and line-construction chain within a different cubic-coordinate context. This original task starts from a y-axis crossing and requests a tangent x-intercept.

hints: Find the coordinates of the $y$-axis crossing point $B$ by substituting $x = 0$ into $y = x^3 - 3x + 2$.
Differentiate the cubic curve to get $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2 - 3$.
Evaluate the gradient at $x = 0$ to get $m = -3$, and form the tangent line equation $y - 2 = -3(x - 0) \implies y = -3x + 2$.
Set $y = 0$ in the tangent equation to find the $x$-coordinate of $C$: $-3x + 2 = 0 \implies x = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the coordinates of $B$ by substituting $x = 0$ into the curve equation:
$$y = (0)^3 - 3(0) + 2 = 2 \implies B(0, 2)$$

Differentiate the curve equation to find the gradient function $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2 - 3$$

Evaluate the gradient of the tangent at $x = 0$:
$$m = \left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=0} = 3(0)^2 - 3 = -3$$

Write the equation of the tangent line passing through $B(0, 2)$ with slope $m = -3$:
$$y - 2 = -3(x - 0) \implies y = -3x + 2$$

Find the $x$-intercept $C$ by setting $y = 0$:
$$0 = -3x + 2 \implies 3x = 2 \implies x = \frac{2}{3}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Evaluates the tangent gradient as $-3$ and forms $y-2=-3x$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: one composite-root derivative leads directly to a tangent equation and its y-axis intercept.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source supports differentiating a composite-root curve and evaluating its gradient at a stated coordinate. This original task uses a tangent y-intercept, rather than a normal equation.

hints: Evaluate the point on the curve at $x = 1$: $y = \sqrt{2(1)+7} = \sqrt{9} = 3 \implies (1, 3)$.
Differentiate $y = (2x+7)^{1/2}$ using the chain rule: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{2}(2x+7)^{-1/2}(2) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2x+7}}$.
Evaluate the slope at $x = 1$: $m = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{9}} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.
Form the tangent line $y - 3 = \dfrac{1}{3}(x - 1)$ and set $x = 0$ to find the $y$-intercept: $y = 3 - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{8}{3}$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the $y$-coordinate of the contact point at $x = 1$:
$$y = \sqrt{2(1)+7} = \sqrt{9} = 3 \implies (1, 3)$$

Differentiate $y = (2x+7)^{1/2}$ using the linear chain rule:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{2}(2x+7)^{-1/2} \times 2 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2x+7}}$$

Evaluate the tangent gradient at $x = 1$:
$$m = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2(1)+7}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{9}} = \frac{1}{3}$$

Write the equation of the tangent line at $(1, 3)$:
$$y - 3 = \frac{1}{3}(x - 1) \implies y = \frac{1}{3}x + \frac{8}{3}$$

Find the $y$-coordinate of $T$ where the tangent meets the $y$-axis by setting $x = 0$:
$$y = \frac{1}{3}(0) + \frac{8}{3} = \frac{8}{3}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Evaluates the tangent gradient as $\dfrac13$ and forms $y-3=\dfrac13(x-1)$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: a reciprocal linear power must be rewritten, differentiated with its signed chain factor, and combined with an evaluated point to give a complete line equation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source combines a reciprocal linear derivative with a line equation. This original task uses a positive numerator, a different inner linear expression, and a direct tangent equation.

hints: Find the point of contact by substituting $x = 1$: $y = \dfrac{2}{3(1)-1} = \dfrac{2}{2} = 1 \implies (1, 1)$.
Rewrite the curve as $y = 2(3x - 1)^{-1}$ and differentiate: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2(-1)(3x - 1)^{-2}(3) = -\dfrac{6}{(3x - 1)^2}$.
Evaluate the gradient at $x = 1$: $m = -\dfrac{6}{(2)^2} = -\dfrac{6}{4} = -\dfrac{3}{2}$.
Form the tangent equation: $y - 1 = -\dfrac{3}{2}(x - 1) \implies y = -\dfrac{3}{2}x + \dfrac{5}{2}$ (or $3x + 2y = 5$).

walkthrough.text:
Find the coordinates of the contact point by substituting $x = 1$ into $y = \dfrac{2}{3x-1}$:
$$y = \frac{2}{3(1) - 1} = \frac{2}{2} = 1 \implies (1, 1)$$

Rewrite the equation in index form and differentiate using the linear chain rule:
$$y = 2(3x - 1)^{-1} \implies \frac{dy}{dx} = 2(-1)(3x - 1)^{-2} \times 3 = -\frac{6}{(3x - 1)^2}$$

Evaluate the tangent gradient at $x = 1$:
$$m = -\frac{6}{(3(1) - 1)^2} = -\frac{6}{2^2} = -\frac{6}{4} = -\frac{3}{2}$$

Construct the equation of the tangent line passing through $(1, 1)$ with slope $m = -\dfrac{3}{2}$:
$$y - 1 = -\frac{3}{2}(x - 1)$$
$$y - 1 = -\frac{3}{2}x + \frac{3}{2} \implies y = -\frac{3}{2}x + \frac{5}{2} \quad (\text{or } 3x + 2y = 5)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds the point $(1,1)$ and tangent gradient $-\frac32$.
Uses the point and gradient to give $y=-\frac32x+\frac52$ or an equivalent equation.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: an unknown coefficient in a cubic curve is recovered from a stated derivative value, after which the full coordinate pair must be returned.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source recovers a polynomial parameter from a stated gradient condition. This original task uses a quadratic parameter term in a cubic curve and requests the resulting contact coordinates.

hints: Differentiate $y = x^3 + kx^2 - 4x$ with respect to $x$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2 + 2kx - 4$.
Substitute $x = 1$ into the derivative and equate to $5$: $3(1)^2 + 2k(1) - 4 = 5 \implies 2k - 1 = 5$.
Solve for $k$: $2k = 6 \implies k = 3$.
Substitute $k = 3$ and $x = 1$ back into the curve to find $y$: $y = (1)^3 + 3(1)^2 - 4(1) = 0 \implies (1, 0)$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the curve $y = x^3 + kx^2 - 4x$ to obtain the gradient function in terms of $k$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2 + 2kx - 4$$

Use the condition that the tangent gradient is $5$ at $x = 1$ to form an equation for $k$:
$$3(1)^2 + 2k(1) - 4 = 5$$
$$3 + 2k - 4 = 5 \implies 2k - 1 = 5$$

Solve for the constant $k$:
$$2k = 6 \implies k = 3$$

Substitute $k = 3$ and $x = 1$ back into the original curve equation to find the $y$-coordinate:
$$y = (1)^3 + 3(1)^2 - 4(1) = 1 + 3 - 4 = 0$$
$$\text{Point of contact: } (1, 0)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes into the curve and states the point $(1,0)$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: a tangent line is given without its point of contact, requiring the learner to equate derivatives to find the contact point.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source identifies points of contact when a tangent line is supplied. This original cubic task reverses the gradient and produces a single point of contact.

hints: The gradient of the tangent line $y = -3x + 3$ is $m = -3$.
Differentiate the curve $y = x^3 - 3x^2 + 2$ to get $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2 - 6x$.
Set $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -3$: $3x^2 - 6x = -3 \implies 3x^2 - 6x + 3 = 0 \implies 3(x - 1)^2 = 0 \implies x = 1$.
Substitute $x = 1$ into either the line or the curve to find $y = -3(1) + 3 = 0 \implies (1, 0)$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the gradient of the tangent line from $y = -3x + 3$:
$$m = -3$$

Differentiate the curve equation $y = x^3 - 3x^2 + 2$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2 - 6x$$

Set the derivative equal to the tangent gradient and solve for $x$:
$$3x^2 - 6x = -3$$
$$3x^2 - 6x + 3 = 0 \implies 3(x^2 - 2x + 1) = 0 \implies 3(x - 1)^2 = 0 \implies x = 1$$

Substitute $x = 1$ into the curve equation to verify and obtain the $y$-coordinate:
$$y = (1)^3 - 3(1)^2 + 2 = 1 - 3 + 2 = 0$$
$$\text{Point of contact: } (1, 0)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets the derivative equal to the tangent gradient $-3$.
Substitutes $x=1$ into the curve to obtain $y=0$ and states the point $(1,0)$.

alternative_routes.description: Equate the supplied line and curve, solve the resulting repeated cubic root, then recover the ordinate.

criteria_mapping.observable: Equates the line and curve to obtain $x^3-3x^2+2=-3x+3$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: differentiating a reciprocal radical term with the chain rule, finding the perpendicular normal slope, forming the normal line, and solving for its x-intercept.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source solves an intercept problem from a fractional normal equation. This original task uses a reciprocal square-root curve and requests the x-axis meeting point.

hints: Find the $y$-coordinate at $x = 1$: $y = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{2(1)+7}} = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{9}} = \dfrac{4}{3} \implies \left(1, \dfrac{4}{3}\right)$.
Rewrite $y = 4(2x+7)^{-1/2}$ and differentiate: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 4\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)(2x+7)^{-3/2}(2) = -4(2x+7)^{-3/2}$.
Form the normal equation $y - \dfrac{4}{3} = \dfrac{27}{4}(x - 1)$ and set $y = 0$: $-\dfrac{4}{3} = \dfrac{27}{4}(x - 1) \implies x - 1 = -\dfrac{16}{81} \implies x = \dfrac{65}{81}$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the coordinates of the point on the curve at $x = 1$:
$$y = \frac{4}{\sqrt{2(1)+7}} = \frac{4}{\sqrt{9}} = \frac{4}{3} \implies \left(1, \frac{4}{3}\right)$$

Express the curve in index form and differentiate using the linear chain rule:
$$y = 4(2x+7)^{-1/2} \implies \frac{dy}{dx} = 4\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)(2x+7)^{-3/2} \times 2 = -4(2x+7)^{-3/2}$$

Evaluate the tangent gradient $m_T$ and the perpendicular normal gradient $m_N$ at $x = 1$:
$$m_T = -4(2(1)+7)^{-3/2} = -4(9)^{-3/2} = -4 \times \frac{1}{27} = -\frac{4}{27}$$
$$m_N = -\frac{1}{m_T} = \frac{27}{4}$$

Write the equation of the normal line through $\left(1, \dfrac{4}{3}\right)$:
$$y - \frac{4}{3} = \frac{27}{4}(x - 1)$$

Find the $x$-intercept of the normal by setting $y = 0$:
$$0 - \frac{4}{3} = \frac{27}{4}(x - 1) \implies x - 1 = -\frac{4}{3} \times \frac{4}{27} = -\frac{16}{81}$$
$$x = 1 - \frac{16}{81} = \frac{65}{81}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Rewrites the curve as $4(2x+7)^{-1/2}$ and differentiates to obtain $-4(2x+7)^{-3/2}$.
Finds the point $(1,\frac43)$ and tangent gradient $-\frac4{27}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: deriving a normal line from a fractional power curve and using its coordinate intercepts to compute an enclosed geometric triangle area.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source derives a normal line from a fractional-power curve and calculates the enclosed region between the normal and coordinate axes. This original task uses a power of 3/2 and requests the full normal equation and geometric area.

hints: Differentiate $y = (x+1)^{3/2}$ using the chain rule: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{3}{2}(x+1)^{1/2}$.
Evaluate the tangent gradient at $x = 3$: $m_T = \dfrac{3}{2}\sqrt{3+1} = \dfrac{3}{2}(2) = 3$.
Find the normal gradient: $m_N = -\dfrac{1}{3}$.
Construct the normal equation through $P(3, 8)$: $y - 8 = -\dfrac{1}{3}(x - 3) \implies y = -\dfrac{1}{3}x + 9$ (or $x + 3y = 27$).

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate $y = (x+1)^{3/2}$ with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{3}{2}(x+1)^{1/2}$$

Evaluate the tangent gradient at $x = 3$:
$$m_T = \left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=3} = \frac{3}{2}\sqrt{3+1} = \frac{3}{2}(2) = 3$$

Determine the normal gradient using $m_N = -\dfrac{1}{m_T}$:
$$m_N = -\frac{1}{3}$$

Write the equation of the normal passing through $P(3, 8)$:
$$y - 8 = -\frac{1}{3}(x - 3)$$
$$y - 8 = -\frac{1}{3}x + 1 \implies y = -\frac{1}{3}x + 9 \quad (\text{or } x + 3y = 27)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Evaluates the tangent gradient at $x=3$ as $\dfrac32\sqrt{4}=3$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding the geometric area of the right triangle formed by the normal line and the coordinate axes.

hints: Find the $y$-intercept of the normal $y = -\dfrac{1}{3}x + 9$ by setting $x = 0 \implies y = 9$.
Find the $x$-intercept of the normal by setting $y = 0 \implies 0 = -\dfrac{1}{3}x + 9 \implies x = 27$.
The triangle formed with the origin is a right-angled triangle with base $27$ and height $9$.
Calculate the area: $\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 27 \times 9 = \dfrac{243}{2} = 121.5$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the $y$-intercept of the normal line $y = -\dfrac{1}{3}x + 9$ by substituting $x = 0$:
$$y = -\frac{1}{3}(0) + 9 = 9 \implies (0, 9)$$

Find the $x$-intercept of the normal line by setting $y = 0$:
$$0 = -\frac{1}{3}x + 9 \implies \frac{1}{3}x = 9 \implies x = 27 \implies (27, 0)$$

The normal line and the coordinate axes form a right-angled triangle with vertices at $(0,0)$, $(27,0)$, and $(0,9)$:
$$\text{Base} = 27, \quad \text{Height} = 9$$

Calculate the area of the right-angled triangle:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 27 \times 9 = \frac{243}{2} = 121.5\text{ square units}$$

ai_rubric.observable: States the area as $\dfrac{243}{2}$ square units ($121.5$).
